headline: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: The committee recommended Bill 141, moving tech park land into residential use, and approved amended Lānaʻi Kōele zoning bills 8 to 1.
meeting.recap: A testifier asked members to wait until after the election.[[0:09:50]] Bill 141 (2026) would move land in the Maui Research and Technology Park into the Residential District.[[0:12:40]] The developer said Maui has a critical need for housing, while demand for commercial space is low.[[0:18:22]] The number of homes allowed would stay at 1,250.[[0:23:27]] The second item was Bills 24 and 25 (2024) on the zoning of Lānaʻi Project District 2, Kōele.[[0:40:12]] The landowner said the plan shrinks the district by 8% and lowers density.[[0:42:10]] The landowner said it would move and preserve two old homes, including the Richardson Home.[[0:57:38]] The landowner said the old bypass road route would affect at least 50 or 60 homes.[[1:16:53]] A council member moved to require quarterly reports for five years, then annual reports.[[1:41:01]] Members passed it 6 to 3 in a roll call vote.[[1:42:17]] Members voted 5 to 4 to strike condition 9, the bypass road requirement.[[2:01:24]] In an 8 to 1 roll call vote, the committee approved the main motion as amended.[[2:09:46]]
meeting.next: Planning said a road built by the landowner and turned over to the County could be considered later in another project. Staff said they understood the intent and would wordsmith the reporting condition.

moments.q: "the department does support the change of zoning"

trackerIssues.title: Maui Research and Technology Park land designation
Lānaʻi Kōele project district zoning and conditions

issues.oneLine: A motion was made to limit quarterly water use reports for Lānaʻi Project District 2, Kōele to five years.
issues.why: The landowner said that without a time limit, reporting could still be going on in 100 years.
issues.next: Planning said future build-out needs a phase two approval from the Lānaʻi Planning Commission, which is when more reporting could be added.
issues.brief: The chair said Planning called a five-year period typical and consistent with past conditions.[[#1]] The landowner said full build-out would take about 10 years.[[#2]]
